short: The settlement that ended the Thirty Years' War and fixed Germany's shape for 150 years.
full:
Two parallel congresses had been negotiating since 1644 - the Catholic powers at Münster, the Protestants and Sweden at Osnabrück - and the treaties were signed on 24 October 1648. Calvinism was recognised alongside Lutheranism and Catholicism, the imperial states were confirmed in effective sovereignty including the right to make their own alliances, and the Dutch Republic and the Swiss Confederation were formally released from the Empire.

Sweden did well out of it. It took Western Pomerania with Stettin, the port of Wismar, and the secularised bishoprics of Bremen and Verden, which gave it control of the mouths of the Oder, Elbe and Weser and seats in the imperial Diet as a German prince in its own right. It also received five million riksdaler to pay off its army. France gained in Alsace, and the Habsburgs kept their hereditary lands but abandoned the attempt to rule the Empire as a unitary Catholic state. Sabaton's "1648" is named for the year of the settlement.
